sights.name: Tivoli Gardens
sights.fact: Opened in 1843, Tivoli is often called the world's second-oldest amusement park still running. The oldest, Bakken from 1583, lies about 10 km to the north.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a tiered pagoda tower beside a wavy roller coaster track on tall supports, standing on a ground line.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Nyhavn canal tour
sights.fact: Nyhavn was dug in the 1670s as a canal linking the harbour to the city centre. Hans Christian Andersen lived in three of its houses.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of narrow gabled townhouses along a canal, with a sailing boat mast and rippling water lines.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Eiffel Tower
sights.fact: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair. It was the tallest structure in the world until 1930.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a lattice tower with curved legs, a wide arch, three platforms and a spire, on a ground line.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Louvre
sights.fact: The Louvre was a royal palace before it opened as a public museum in 1793. Its glass pyramid entrance was completed in 1989.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a gridded glass pyramid in front of a long palace wing with rows of windows and a ground line.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Tower of London
sights.fact: The Tower of London was founded after the Norman Conquest of 1066. Today it holds the Crown Jewels of the United Kingdom.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a square keep with two domed corner turrets and battlements, behind a low crenellated wall with a gate.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: British Museum
sights.fact: Founded in 1753, the British Museum opened to the public in 1759. It is home to the Rosetta Stone.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a classical temple front with a triangular pediment, a row of columns and wide steps.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Colosseum
sights.fact: The Colosseum was completed in AD 80 under Emperor Titus. It could hold an estimated 50,000 spectators.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a curved amphitheatre wall with three tiers of arches and a broken, uneven top on one side.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Vatican Museums
sights.fact: The Vatican Museums trace their origins to Pope Julius II in the early 1500s. Their route includes the Sistine Chapel, whose ceiling Michelangelo painted from 1508 to 1512.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a high wall with an arched gateway, with a large ribbed dome and lantern rising behind it.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Topkapı Palace
sights.fact: Topkapı Palace was the main residence of the Ottoman sultans for nearly 400 years. It became a museum in 1924.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of an arched palace gate flanked by two towers with pointed conical roofs, on a crenellated wall.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Galata Tower
sights.fact: The Galata Tower was built in 1348 as part of the walls of the Genoese colony of Galata.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a round stone tower with arched windows, a top gallery and a tall conical roof, on a ground line.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Statue of Liberty
sights.fact: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France and was dedicated in 1886. Its copper skin turned green over time as a patina formed.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a robed statue with a spiked crown and raised torch, standing on a tall stepped pedestal.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Empire State Building
sights.fact: The Empire State Building opened in 1931 after just over 13 months of construction. It was the tallest building in the world until 1970.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a stepped skyscraper with several setbacks, vertical window bands and a slender spire on top.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Senso-ji
sights.fact: Senso-ji is Tokyo's oldest temple, traditionally dated to 628. Visitors enter through the Kaminarimon, or Thunder Gate.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a temple gate with a wide curved roof, four pillars and a large paper lantern hanging in the middle.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Tokyo Skytree
sights.fact: Tokyo Skytree is 634 metres tall and opened in 2012. It is the tallest tower in Japan.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a tall tapering lattice tower with two box-shaped observation decks and an antenna on top.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Sydney Opera House
sights.fact: The Sydney Opera House, designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon, opened in 1973. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of overlapping curved shell roofs on a wide stepped platform, with water lines below.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team

sights.name: Harbour Bridge
sights.fact: The Sydney Harbour Bridge opened in 1932. Its steel arch spans 503 metres, and it is nicknamed 'the Coathanger'.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a steel arch bridge with vertical hangers, a flat deck and stone pylons at each end, over water.
sights.author: Claude (AI), for the Worldbound team
